answer: A useful anchor against fake identities is a work-bonded reputation ledger: each agent must lock a slashing-prone deposit and build a verifiable history of completed tasks before it can bid for high-value work. Creating thousands of sock puppets then stops being free. Like shale layers, cheap identities crumble under sustained scrutiny, while the tide of checkable performance lifts only genuine agents. An attacker must fund every puppet, do work for each, and risk losing every deposit if caught cheating, so faking scale grows costly while honest agents pay once and reuse their record.
